Chicken Tagine with Preserved Lemon & Olives

55 minMediumServes 1–4

Prep — Ras el Hanout Spice Blend

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Chicken thighs, bone-in150g300g450g600g
Onion, sliced30g60g90g120g
Garlic cloves1234
Fresh ginger, grated¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Ras el hanout¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Ground turmeric⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Saffron threadspinchpinch2 pinches2 pinches
Cinnamon stick¼½¾1
Olive oil5ml10ml15ml20ml
Chicken stock or water60ml120ml180ml240ml
Preserved lemon, quartered¼½¾1
Green or violet olives20g40g60g80g
Saltpinchpinch¼ tsp¼ tsp
Cilantro & parsley, chopped5g10g15g20g

Steps

  1. Warm the olive oil in a wide heavy pot and cook the sliced onion 4-5 minutes until soft.
  2. Stir in the garlic, ginger, ras el hanout, turmeric, saffron, and cinnamon stick, cooking 1 minute until fragrant.
  3. Nestle the chicken into the onions and spices, turning to coat.
  4. Pour in the stock or water, cover, and simmer low 40-45 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
  5. Add the preserved lemon rind and olives, and simmer uncovered 10 more minutes to thicken the sauce.
  6. Taste and season lightly with salt (preserved lemon and olives are already salty).
  7. Sprinkle with chopped cilantro and parsley.
  8. Serve hot, spooning the sauce over the chicken, with warm bread or couscous.

Harira (Moroccan Lentil & Chickpea Soup)

70 min (mostly hands-off)EasyServes 1–4

Prep — Home-Simmered Harira

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Brown or green lentils, rinsed30g60g90g120g
Chickpeas, soaked (or canned, drained)30g60g90g120g
Crushed tomatoes60g120g180g240g
Onion, finely chopped20g40g60g80g
Celery, finely chopped10g20g30g40g
Olive oil5ml10ml15ml20ml
Fresh ginger, grated¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Ground black pepper⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Ground turmeric⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Ground cinnamonpinchpinch⅛ tsp¼ tsp
Saffron threadspinchpinch2 pinches2 pinches
All-purpose flour (for tedouira)5g10g15g20g
Water250ml500ml750ml1000ml
Saltpinchpinch⅛ tsp¼ tsp
Cilantro & parsley, chopped5g10g15g20g
Vermicelli (optional)10g20g30g40g
Lemon wedges (to serve)¼½¾1

Steps

  1. Cook the onion and celery in a little oil 4-5 minutes until soft.
  2. Stir in the ginger, black pepper, turmeric, cinnamon, and saffron, cooking 30 seconds until fragrant.
  3. Add the crushed tomatoes, lentils, chickpeas, and water, and bring to a boil.
  4. Reduce to a simmer, cover partway, and cook 45-60 minutes until the lentils and chickpeas are tender.
  5. If using, stir in the vermicelli and simmer 5-8 minutes more.
  6. Whisk the flour with a little cold water into a smooth, thin tedouira.
  7. Drizzle the tedouira into the simmering soup while stirring, then simmer 5 more minutes until velvety.
  8. Taste and season with salt.
  9. Stir in the chopped cilantro and parsley.
  10. Ladle into bowls and serve with lemon wedges and dates on the side.

Kefta Tagine (Spiced Meatball Tagine in Tomato Sauce)

45 minMediumServes 1–4

Prep — Kofta, Chickpeas & Couscous

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Ground beef or lamb120g240g360g480g
Onion, grated (for meatballs)15g30g45g60g
Garlic cloves1234
Parsley & cilantro, chopped5g10g15g20g
Ground cumin⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Sweet paprika⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Ground cinnamonpinchpinch⅛ tsp¼ tsp
Olive oil5ml10ml15ml20ml
Onion, finely chopped (for sauce)20g40g60g80g
Ground ginger⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Crushed tomatoes100g200g300g400g
Eggs1234
Cilantro, chopped (garnish)5g10g15g20g

Steps

  1. Mix the ground meat with grated onion, half the garlic, parsley, cilantro, cumin, paprika, and cinnamon.
  2. Roll the mixture into small, walnut-sized meatballs.
  3. Cook the finely chopped onion in olive oil 4-5 minutes until soft.
  4. Stir in the remaining garlic and ginger, then add the crushed tomatoes and a splash of water, simmering uncovered 10 minutes.
  5. Lower the meatballs into the sauce, cover, and cook 15-20 minutes until cooked through.
  6. Make small wells in the sauce between the meatballs.
  7. Crack an egg into each well, cover, and cook 7-10 minutes until the whites set but yolks stay runny.
  8. Sprinkle with chopped cilantro.
  9. Serve straight from the pot with warm crusty bread.

Moroccan Fish Chermoula

30 min (+30 min marinate)EasyServes 1–4

Prep — Fresh Parsley for the Chermoula

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
White fish fillets (hake, cod, or sea bass)120g240g360g480g
Fresh cilantro, chopped10g20g30g40g
Fresh parsley, chopped10g20g30g40g
Garlic cloves1234
Ground cumin⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Sweet paprika⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Lemon juice10ml20ml30ml40ml
Olive oil15ml30ml45ml60ml
Bell pepper, sliced (optional)20g40g60g80g
Tomato, sliced (optional)20g40g60g80g
Lemon wedges (to serve)¼½¾1

Steps

  1. Blend the cilantro, parsley, garlic, cumin, paprika, lemon juice, and olive oil into a coarse chermoula paste.
  2. Rub the fish with about two-thirds of the chermoula and marinate in the fridge 30 minutes to 2 hours.
  3. Warm a little oil in a wide pan and, if using, cook the bell pepper and tomato 3-4 minutes until softened.
  4. Lay the marinated fish in the pan and cook 3-4 minutes per side until it flakes easily.
  5. Spoon the remaining chermoula over the fish during the last minute of cooking.
  6. Lift the fish and vegetables onto a plate.
  7. Serve warm with lemon wedges and crusty bread or rice.

Moroccan Chicken with Chickpeas & Apricots

55 minMediumServes 1–4

Prep — Soaked & Dried Chickpeas

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Chicken thighs, bone-in or boneless140g280g420g560g
Onion, sliced30g60g90g120g
Olive oil5ml10ml15ml20ml
Garlic cloves1234
Fresh ginger, grated¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Ground cinnamon⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Ground coriander⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Ground turmeric⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Saffron threadspinchpinch2 pinches2 pinches
Honey5ml10ml15ml20ml
Chickpeas, cooked or canned (drained)40g80g120g160g
Dried apricots20g40g60g80g
Chicken stock or water80ml160ml240ml320ml
Salt⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Toasted almonds (garnish)5g10g15g20g
Cilantro, chopped5g10g15g20g

Steps

  1. Cook the onion in a little oil 4-5 minutes until soft.
  2. Stir in the garlic, ginger, cinnamon, coriander, turmeric, and saffron, cooking 1 minute until fragrant.
  3. Nestle the chicken into the spiced onions, turning to coat.
  4. Add the stock or water, bring to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook low 25-30 minutes.
  5. Stir in the honey, chickpeas, and dried apricots, and simmer uncovered 15-20 minutes more until the chicken is fully cooked.
  6. Taste and season with salt as needed.
  7. Scatter the toasted almonds and chopped cilantro over the top.
  8. Serve hot with couscous or warm bread.

Couscous with Seven Vegetables

75 minMediumServes 1–4

Prep — The Traditional Couscoussière

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Medium couscous (semolina)60g120g180g240g
Bone-in chicken or lamb pieces (for broth)100g200g300g400g
Carrot, cut into chunks30g60g90g120g
Turnip, cut into chunks25g50g75g100g
Zucchini, cut into chunks30g60g90g120g
Pumpkin or butternut squash, cut into chunks30g60g90g120g
Cabbage, cut into wedges25g50g75g100g
Tomato, chopped20g40g60g80g
Chickpeas, soaked or canned (drained)20g40g60g80g
Onion, chopped20g40g60g80g
Olive oil5ml10ml15ml20ml
Ground ginger⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Ground turmeric⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Saffron threadspinchpinch2 pinches2 pinches
Butter (or smen)5g10g15g20g
Water or stock200ml400ml600ml800ml
Raisins (optional garnish)5g10g15g20g

Steps

  1. Cook the onion with ginger, turmeric, and saffron in a little oil 2-3 minutes, then add the tomato and cook until saucy.
  2. Add the chicken or lamb and water to cover, bring to a boil, and skim off any foam.
  3. Add the chickpeas, cover partway, and simmer 30-40 minutes.
  4. Spread the dry couscous in a wide dish, drizzle with water and oil, and rub between your palms to separate every grain.
  5. Steam the couscous uncovered over the simmering broth 15-20 minutes.
  6. Tip the couscous back into the dish, drizzle with warm salted water, and fluff it between your palms; repeat the steaming once more for the best texture.
  7. Add the carrot and turnip to the broth and simmer 10 minutes.
  8. Add the zucchini, pumpkin, and cabbage, and simmer 10-15 more minutes until tender.
  9. Mound the fluffed couscous on a platter and dot with butter, tossing to melt through.
  10. Arrange the vegetables and chickpeas over the couscous, scatter raisins on top, and ladle a little broth over everything.
  11. Serve the extra broth on the side for spooning over individual plates.

Lamb Tagine with Apricots & Almonds

2 hr 15 min (mostly hands-off)MediumServes 1–4

Prep — Dried Apricots

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Lamb shoulder, cubed130g260g390g520g
Olive oil5ml10ml15ml20ml
Onion, sliced30g60g90g120g
Garlic cloves1234
Fresh ginger, grated¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Ground cinnamon⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Ground cumin⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Saltpinch¼ tsp¼ tsp½ tsp
Saffron threadspinchpinch2 pinches2 pinches
Honey5ml10ml15ml20ml
Dried apricots20g40g60g80g
Blanched almonds10g20g30g40g
Sesame seeds (garnish)pinch¼ tsp¼ tsp½ tsp
Water or stock100ml200ml300ml400ml
Cilantro & parsley, chopped5g10g15g20g

Steps

  1. Season the lamb with cinnamon, cumin, saffron, and a pinch of salt.
  2. Brown the lamb in batches in a little oil, 3-4 minutes per side, then set aside.
  3. Cook the onion 4-5 minutes until soft, then add garlic and ginger for 1 minute.
  4. Return the lamb to the pot with the water or stock, cover, and simmer low 1½-2 hours until fork-tender.
  5. Stir in the honey and dried apricots, and simmer uncovered 30-45 minutes more until plump and the sauce thickens.
  6. Toast the almonds in a dry pan 3-4 minutes until golden.
  7. Taste and season with salt.
  8. Spoon onto a platter, scatter with toasted almonds, sesame seeds, cilantro, and parsley.
  9. Serve hot with couscous or crusty bread.

Moroccan Orange & Cinnamon Salad (Fenjaan) (Bonus)

15 min (+15 min chill)EasyServes 1–4

Prep — A Fresh Navel Orange

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Navel oranges, peeled & pith removed1234
Ground cinnamon⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Orange blossom water¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Honey5ml10ml15ml20ml
Fresh mint leaves (garnish)2468
Toasted almonds or chopped dates (optional garnish)5g10g15g20g

Steps

  1. Peel the oranges down to the flesh, removing all the white pith.
  2. Slice the oranges crosswise into thin rounds, catching any juice, and arrange on a plate.
  3. Whisk the collected juice with the orange blossom water and honey.
  4. Drizzle the juice mixture evenly over the orange slices.
  5. Sprinkle the cinnamon over the top.
  6. Scatter with mint leaves and almonds or dates, if using.
  7. Chill at least 15 minutes before serving.
